summary: I confirmed the builder's verification claims. All five tsc configs are clean. Vitest gives the same counts the builder reported: core 1050 tests in 75 files, webview 314 in 19, extension 204 in 22 (run with --no-cache). The five runner files I ran with real Lean all pass. I isolated the work by comparing it with after_slice_2b2.patch: 15 files changed. These parts are correct and I found no problems in them: the R2-1 revert fix and its tests, the protocol validators and the `session` light check, endorsements in the build, `endorsementHash` and the sidecar helpers, and the host's `not-yet` default. The new base mask has real defects, and I reproduced each one with esbuild-bundled scripts in my scratch dir that run the repo's own code. (1) A hidden lemma placed directly below a pinned card's block turns that card code-less on the masked board. (2) The parser's TL013 hint (and TL014) survives the mask: TL013 names a hidden proof-phase declaration, and TL014 reveals that a hidden `mutual` follows the card. (3) A comment Claude writes above a hidden lemma between another card's statement and its `.holds` appears in that card's masked code; the unmasked build does not show it. (4) `maskedModel` drops `endorsements` and `lakefile`. (5) `withoutHidden` handles a hidden `mutual` with its inner declarations in the wrong order and deletes the person's own text after it. Findings 1–3 break §4.7's rule that no hidden proof text reaches a graph, and the non-interference property. The step limits accept each of those states. Nothing in the repo changed during my review: the snapdiff before and after is byte-identical, the .vite-temp folders are empty, and no /tmp/telelean-* folder exists.

findings.problem: When a block's `adjacentDecl` is left out by the mask, `maskFiles` replaces the whole binding with `{ mode: 'none' }`, even for a PINNED block. The parser records `adjacentDecl` for pinned blocks too (`bindBlock` spreads `position` into the pinned binding). So a hidden proof-phase lemma written directly below a pinned card's block, above that card's statement, unbinds the card in the masked build: it shows informal, with no statement, no code and proof `none`. B and the working copy both show it formalized. This is a wrong board under the mask, and it tells the two outcomes apart (lemma placed there or not). The step limits accept the state: the `lean:` line and the binding are unchanged, and the only below-block rule covers new axioms.
findings.evidence: Scratch experiment exp3.ts inserts `theorem helper_above : True := trivial` right after the target's block `-/` (ledger `created(…, 'proof')`). Unmasked W: `pinned Spyro.cynder_not_good formalized`. Masked: `none undefined informal {"kind":"none"}`. B: `pinned … formalized {"kind":"pending"}`. The same happens with another card (new-spyro-pg: masked `none … informal`, B `pinned … assumed`).
findings.fix: Reset the binding only for mode `adjacent`. In maskFiles: `if (now !== undefined) binding.adjacentDecl = now; else if (binding.mode === 'adjacent') binding = { mode: 'none' }; else delete binding.adjacentDecl;`. Add a mask test with a hidden lemma directly below a pinned card's block (the target and another card): the card stays formalized, with B's code and status, and the stripped graph equals the one without the lemma.

findings.where: packages/core/src/project/build.ts:287-311 (maskFiles: gapDecl re-indexing and the diagnostics filter); test packages/core/test/review/mask.test.ts:623
findings.problem: Parser hints that sit on a block's marker but describe the declaration after it are kept, even when that declaration is left out. TL013 reads "This node is code-less, but `‹name›` follows after a blank line". It names a hidden proof-phase lemma that Claude placed after a code-less card and a blank line. TL014 says that a hidden `mutual` follows a code-less card directly. maskFiles deletes `gapDecl` (or resets the binding) but filters diagnostics only by `inside(d.span.start)` of the hidden spans, and the marker span is never inside one. This leaks a hidden declaration's name into the masked graph. Builder decision 10 says no stage can hold this state, but that holds only for the adjacent case. The gap case leaves the card's binding as `none`, so the step limits accept it; the readiness rule only checks selected cards. The test at mask.test.ts:623 excludes TL013 from its assertion, so it cannot catch this.
findings.evidence: exp1.ts (a): B = B1 plus a code-less card at the end of Main. W = PROVED1 plus that card, a blank line, and `theorem secret_helper_lemma` (ledger proof). The masked graph contains ["TL013","spyro-is-blue","This node is code-less, but `secret_helper_lemma` follows after a blank line: remove the blank line to attach it."]. B's graph has no TL013. exp2.ts (t): a hidden `mutual` directly below the same card leaves TL014 "…(a `mutual` block holds several declarations…)" on the masked board, and B has none.
findings.fix: In maskFiles, when a block's `gapDecl` or (for a block with mode `none`) its `adjacentDecl` points at a left-out declaration, drop that block's TL013 and TL014 diagnostics. Ideally re-derive them from the masked declarations: the next kept declaration after the block, with only whitespace between once the hidden spans are removed. Then the masked board shows B's hint, never one about hidden content. Add tests for: a code-less card, a blank line, then a hidden lemma (no hidden name anywhere in the JSON); and a hidden `mutual` directly below a code-less card (no TL014). Remove the `d.code !== 'TL013'` exclusion at mask.test.ts:623.

findings.problem: When hidden declarations sit between another card's statement and its `.holds`, maskedCode deletes only their spans (`deletionEdit`) and accepts the rest of the gap if it holds only blanks and comments. A comment that Claude wrote with the hidden lemma (C5 attaches it to the lemma, so it is part of the hidden item) therefore stays in the composed one-stretch code, and that code goes into the masked graph. The unmasked two-piece code would not even show it. Hidden proof-phase text reaches the graph, against §4.7's "no hidden proof text reaches a graph", and the proved and not-proved outcomes give different SessionViews. The step limits accept such a comment: sessionRules attaches the added line to the lemma via `attachedTo`.
findings.evidence: exp1.ts (b): W = PROVED1 with `-- secret: the proof of cynder_not_good goes through this` followed by `theorem between : True := trivial` inserted between `abbrev cynder_dark_past` and its `.holds` (ledger proof). Masked code: "…abbrev cynder_dark_past : Prop := HasDarkPast cynder\n-- secret: the proof of cynder_not_good goes through this\naxiom cynder_dark_past.holds : cynder_dark_past". B's code has no such line. The unmasked code is two pieces, without the comment.
findings.fix: Compose such a card's code from B's layout, as is already done for targets. In projectMaskOf, for every card whose statement and `.holds` have B's texts, record B's joint (`codeJoint` on B's statement and `.holds`) or B's two pieces. maskedCode then uses `stmtText + jointB + holdsText`, and the working copy's gap is never read. That also removes the tell when a target's moved `.holds` lands inside another card's stretch. At minimum, also delete the comment lines that `compareTexts` attaches to each hidden declaration. Add a test: a comment above a hidden lemma between another card's statement and `.holds` gives B's code exactly.

findings.problem: maskedModel rebuilds the working copy with only `files`, `fileHashes`, `facts`, `library` and `mask`. It drops the `endorsements` input this sub-slice added, and the `lakefile` input. A ProjectModel does not record them, and maskedModel's input has no field for them. Once 2f passes endorsements.json, the hidden-results board 2c2 builds with maskedModel will flag every endorsed definition, and every card that uses one, with `definitional-choice` ("needs your endorsement"). B and the working copy do not. The TL110 auto-implicit warning is also lost. No hidden content leaks, but the masked board's vocabulary chips disagree with the working copy's, which §4.7 says keeps statements and vocabulary.
findings.evidence: exp2.ts (d): with `{ Spyro: [{ name: 'Spyro.DarkChar', textHash: endorsementHash(code) }] }`, B and W built with endorsements give flags [[],[]] (the item, then the card). `maskedModel({ current: W, base: B, mask })` gives [["definitional-choice"],["definitional-choice"]].
findings.fix: Add optional `endorsements` and `lakefile` to maskedModel's input and pass them through to buildProjectModel (2c2's SessionViewInput or the runner supplies them). Add a mask test: an endorsed definition is not flagged on the masked board.

findings.problem: For a hidden `mutual`, maskFiles pushes both the `mutual` span and its inner declarations' spans. withoutHidden deletes the spans in descending start order, so the inner declarations go first. Then `deletionEdit(t, mutualSpan)` runs with the `mutual`'s original end offset, which is now stale. It deletes past the `mutual` into the rest of the gap, up to the clamped `.holds` start, removing the person's own text that follows it. The masked code then differs from B's, the very layout that LeanOps' removal and decision 3 promise.
findings.evidence:
exp2.ts (c): B has `-- the person's own note` between `abbrev cynder_dark_past` and its `.holds`. W adds a hidden `mutual` (even_x, odd_x) above that note. Masked code: "…HasDarkPast cynder
axiom cynder_dark_past.holds : cynder_dark_past" (the note is gone). B's code keeps "
-- the person's own note
".
findings.fix: In withoutHidden, merge the spans first and delete only the outermost ones: skip any span contained in another, or sort by start and coalesce overlapping spans. If C3's B-layout fix is taken, this path goes away. Add a test with a hidden `mutual` between a card's statement and `.holds`, followed by a comment: the masked code equals B's.

findings.problem: The new `default` answers every unrouted run message with `not-yet`. This removes the exhaustiveness check that made tsc fail for an unrouted run message. A future M2 or slice-2 run message that someone forgets to route would answer "Not built yet (slice 2)" without any compile error.
findings.fix: Replace `default` with explicit `case` labels for the ten SESSION_MESSAGE_TYPES (each answering `not-yet`). The switch then stays exhaustive, and 2d–2f remove each case as they route it.
